h: Batting, wizards and a canal walk
p: Here's a tip: book your session for when you know your group will be fresh rather than squeezing it in after a long day of shopping. Cricket nets are more fun when everyone has the energy to swing, and the competitive edge stays sharp. Bring a water bottle, wear clothes you can twist and turn in, and start on a gentle setting to get your eye in before cranking it up.

Watford has a surprising amount to pair with it. Big-name fans will know that the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London, home of the Making of Harry Potter, is just up the road at Leavesden. It needs booking well in advance and most of a day in its own right, but if you're staying locally, a cricket session the day before or after makes a fun change of pace.

Closer to the centre, the Watford Palace Theatre puts on drama, comedy and a family panto, and the Atria shopping centre is the place for high-street shopping and food. Football fans will want to know that Vicarage Road, home of Watford FC, is a short walk from the town centre. For something calmer, the Grand Union Canal towpath through Cassiobury Park is a gorgeous walk, passing locks and narrowboats, and the park's paddling pools are a summer favourite with young families. With all that on your doorstep, the nets are an easy addition to a longer stay.
